Solutions 2 and 3 give the same value, and I judge it most likely correct, though I did not fully prove it is the minimum. Solution 1 gives √5, which I could not support.

**Checking the shared value.** Take f(z) = z³ − z² + z + 1. On |z| = 1 its autocorrelation coefficients are A₁ = −1, A₂ = 0, A₃ = 1, so

|f(e^{iθ})|² = 4 − 2cos θ + 2cos 3θ.

With x = cos θ, this becomes 4 + 8x³ − 8x. Its derivative vanishes at x = ±1/√3, and the maximum is at x = −1/√3:

|f|² = 4 + 16√3/9 ≈ 7.08.

The other candidate I tried, f = z³ + z² + z − 1, gives the same value, and f = z³ + iz² + iz + 1 gives a larger one (8). This supports 4 + 16√3/9 as the minimum of the maximum, at least for these cases.

**Equivalence of the two forms.** 2√(9+4√3)/3 = √(36+16√3)/3, since 4(9+4√3) = 36+16√3. So Solutions 2 and 3 agree.

**Solution 1.** It offers no derivation. A bound of |f|² ≤ 5 would require a nearly flat modulus on the circle, which seems implausible given the nonzero third-harmonic term of amplitude 2. I could not support it.

**What I did not verify.** Solutions 2 and 3 argue by perturbation that A₂ = 0 is optimal. That argument is only partial, so I am relying on my own spot checks and on the two solutions agreeing.

CHOICE: 2
